newsitem.title: FRANCE: Corsican separatist surrenders to French police.
newsitem.headline: Corsican separatist surrenders to French police.

text.p: A Corsican separatist surrendered to police during the night, the third suspected guerrilla to do so in recent weeks, police said on Tuesday.
Andre Franceschi, a member of A Cuncolta Nazuinalista, was wanted in connection with a machine-gun attack last week on a hotel in Aregno.

Two leaders of the group have surrendered recently. A Cuncolta is the political arm of the Corsican National Liberation Front (FLNC)-Historic Wing, which has been battling for two decades for greater autonomy for the Mediterranean island.
The FLNC staged several bombings on the French mainland recently, including one on Prime Minister Alain Juppe's mayoral office in Bordeaux.

Police said later on Tuesday they had arrested another activist close to Cuncolta, named as Charles Agostini and suspected of involvement in an attack on a tax office and on the law courts in Nimes on the southern French mainland.
Police said six bullets were fired early on Tuesday at the home of a government worker in Porto Vecchio. There were no injuries and no one has yet claimed responsibility.
